sentences.note: Framing sentence naming the paper's three central bets: guilt from responsible social choice, its anterior-insula substrate, and a substrate tracking responsibility for the partner's outcomes.
Two-study design (one behavioural, one during fMRI); states the design, not a finding.
The three conditions (Social, Partner, Solo) that structure every result; described here, asserted as a scope claim in the graph.
The lottery structure; a method description with no paper-specific finding.
Outcome display and momentary-happiness sampling; method description.
The manipulation-check finding that happiness tracks both own and partner outcomes; combines the two reward-tracking claims.

The core behavioural guilt effect. The abstract states the interaction but drops the control that it held regardless of the participant's own outcome, which dissociates guilt from inequality aversion.
The left anterior insula cluster. The abstract does not mention that convergence with the published Yu et al. guilt signature holds only in aggregate and not at the individual level.
The insula–right IFG gPPI finding and its interpretation, stated together.

Compresses the computational-modelling result. The abstract does not surface that the responsibility-weighted partner-RPE term (social_pRPE) was the reliably positive one, nor the model comparison that selected it.
The left STS cluster tracking partner RPEs that followed participant choices.
Closing claim; states that the paper has identified neural mechanisms of guilt and responsibility.
